description_full: PTC Therapeutics, Inc., a biopharmaceutical company, focuses on the discovery, development, and commercialization of medicines to children and adults living with rare disorders in the United States and internationally. The company provides Translarna and Emflaza for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy; Upstaza to treat aromatic l-amino acid decarboxylas (AADC) deficiency, a central nervous system disorder; Tegsedi and Waylivra for the treatment of rare diseases; and Evrysdi to treat spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in adults and children. Its development pipeline products include Sepiapterin for the treatment of phenylketonuria; PTC518 splicing platform, which is being developed for the treatment of Huntington's disease; and inflammation and ferroptosis platforms, including vatiquinone to treat Friedreich's ataxia. The company distributes its products through third-party distributors. It has collaborations with F. Hoffman-La Roche Ltd., Hoffman-La Roche Inc., the SMA Foundation, National Taiwan University, Akcea Therapeutics, Inc., and Shiratori Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. The company has license and collaboration agreement with Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation to develop PTC518 Huntington's disease program. It markets Upstaza, a gene therapy with the brand name Kebilidi in the United States. PTC Therapeutics, Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Warren, New Jersey.

financial_summary: PTC Therapeutics, Inc. is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $5.5B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +35% over the past three years and +47% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +15.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -60% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $702M in free cash flow — roughly 41 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.04× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 7.3% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 5.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
